inputs.original_text:
Look at what happens when bureaucratic incompetence and institutional foot-dragging collide with basic civic order. We are looking at a situation where over 58 lakh names were deleted during a revision exercise in West Bengal. Now, instead of maintaining stability and ensuring a proper, orderly process, the system bogs itself down. 

We are told that tribunals for voters missing from West Bengal's electoral rolls are not yet operational. Even though the Supreme Court directed these tribunals, their functioning details are pending because the state government and Calcutta High Court are just bogged down discussing locations. Meanwhile, the software for voters to challenge rulings is ready, but what good is an appeal mechanism when the actual institutions meant to deliver justice aren't even functioning? 

This is a complete abdication of responsibility by the authorities, showing exactly why we cannot rely on progressive administrative mismanagement to keep our society functioning. When the pillars of law and order fail to execute their basic duties, it is the ordinary, hardworking citizens who pay the price while the machinery of government grinds to a halt over mere logistics.
inputs.modified_text:
Look at the absolute state of civic administration today. Over 58 lakh names were deleted during a revision exercise in West Bengal, and how do the authorities handle it? By dragging their feet and wallowing in bureaucratic incompetence. 

The Supreme Court directed that tribunals be set up for voters missing from West Bengal's electoral rolls, but they are not yet operational. Why? Because the state government and Calcutta High Court are completely bogged down just discussing locations. Meanwhile, we are told that the software for voters to challenge rulings is ready, but what good is an appeal mechanism when the actual institutions meant to deliver justice aren't even functioning? 

This is a complete abdication of responsibility by the authorities, showing exactly why we cannot rely on progressive administrative mismanagement to keep our society functioning. When the pillars of law and order fail to execute their basic duties, it is the ordinary, hardworking citizens who pay the price while the machinery of government grinds to a halt over mere logistics. Tradition, order, and basic duty are being sacrificed for endless dithering, and it is time for accountability.
